title: Dangling Local
goal: Return a freshly built id. One of these can never work — and one pays double.
hints: The string is BORN here — there is nothing in the caller's world for a returned reference to point at.
When the function creates the value, the function must hand over ownership.
explanation: The borrowing version can never compile: `id` dies at the closing brace, so `&id` would dangle (E0515 — and no lifetime annotation can fix a value that stops existing). When a function CREATES data, it must return ownership: `-> String`, moving the fresh value out. The clone dance also returns ownership but copies the string it already owned for no reason. Zero-copy returns are for views into inputs; freshly built values are moved out, not borrowed.
